Minor deductions: pages bypass data.js and call fetchJson directly with inline any-typed shaping, and the home page couples to home.js via hardcoded element ids.

app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:84-88, app/src/pages/types/[name].astro:85-89, app/src/pages/abilities/[name].astro:56-60 — 'N Pokémon + card-grid' section triplicated

abstraction_design.rationale: The existing abstractions (PokemonCard, TypeBadge, EvolutionNode, format/data helpers) are well-shaped for their variation, but pages don't stretch: a similar-but-different feature either copies a monolithic page or copies a data helper. That's classic 3-tier copy-paste creep rather than flag-parameter over-generalization.

findings.issue: Near-duplicate of pokemonRefsToSpecies from app/src/lib/data.js:56-79 (same id-exclusion, fetch, species dedup, sort) differing only by the hidden-ability flag; any change to the mapping must be made in both places.
findings.suggestion: Extend pokemonRefsToSpecies to return the raw entries (e.g. map to {id, name, source}) or accept a mapper, and have the ability page derive 'hidden' from the returned entries.

findings.issue: Sprite URL is synthesized from the species id (spriteFor) instead of using the fetched Pokémon's sprites.front_default, so cards can show wrong sprites for species whose default Pokémon differs, and a real fix must plumb a sprite field through data.js, the abilities inline mapping, index.astro and PokemonCard.
findings.suggestion: Have list-producing helpers carry an optional sprite URL from the Pokémon record (falling back to the pattern), and give PokemonCard an optional sprite prop overriding the pattern.

findings.issue: Filter query-param building is duplicated between the server pageUrl helper and the client script (app/public/js/home.js:15-18), so changing defaults/param names means two synchronized edits.
findings.suggestion: Render the canonical URLs into data-* attributes (or a JSON script tag) the client script reads, or derive params from the form alone in one shared place.

findings.issue: Pervasive 'any' typing in page frontmatter (also moves/types/abilities pages); the shapes flowing between fetch and markup are untyped, so edits require re-reading the whole page to know a field exists.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the API responses and the derived 'data' objects in lib (e.g. lib/types.ts) and use them in pages and component props.

findings.issue: The try/catch-404-with-NotFound-fallback pattern is repeated in four dynamic routes (moves:41, abilities:38, types:23/45, pokemon:126).
findings.suggestion: Extract a helper like withResource(name, fetcher) that returns {data}|{notFound} and sets Astro.response.status, so the pattern lives once.

findings.issue: The 'N Pokémon + count + card-grid' section markup is triplicated (moves:84-88, abilities:56-60), so adding e.g. sorting or an empty-state to card lists means three edits.
findings.suggestion: Extract a PokemonGrid component (count text + optional empty state + ul.card-grid) used by move, ability and type pages.

findings.issue: Shared selectors mix per-feature styles (.plain-list only used by the abilities section, grouped with .evo-tree), so feature removal leaves dead CSS.
findings.suggestion: Use Astro's scoped styles in components for component-specific rules, or split global.css per feature/page section.

findings.issue: Only dist/ and node_modules/ are ignored; the generated .astro/ types directory is committed to the repo.

summary: A tidy, idiomatic Astro 7 SSR app: every card list renders through one component, all API knowledge sits in one lib module, and pages are readable frontmatter-plus-markdown files with organized CSS. The main editability costs are duplicated species-mapping logic (ability page copies a data helper), synthesized sprite URLs that would need plumbing through several data paths to fix, and monolithic per-resource pages with an any-typed internal shape. Extending or removing features is generally a handful of findable edits rather than a refactor.
